Reviewing the analysis and the peer responses, all models correctly identify that the statute creates a facial classification based on sex (gender) by requiring male and female students to live in separate facilities. Under the Equal Protection Clause, sex-based classifications are subject to intermediate scrutiny. 

Under intermediate scrutiny, the burden of persuasion rests on the state to prove that the classification is substantially related to an important governmental interest, which matches option (C). The peer responses accurately reinforce this reasoning and properly dismiss the alternative options regarding fundamental rights (privacy or association) and rational basis review.

Final answer: C
